device: none: no model is loaded; dense vectors and cross-encoder scores are read from the harness caches and sparse retrievers are refitted on CPU

retriever_details.card_notes: config_sentence_transformers.json: prompts {} and default_prompt_name null, so no prefix; modules: Transformer (BertModel, hidden 1024) + mean Pooling, no Normalize module; sentence_bert_config.json max_seq_length 128 (production value, kept so vectors equal the build_udvs cache); trained with AnglELoss on STS.

harness.rows: per-query rows written by utils.retrieval_experiments run under <run.output_dir>/<run_name>/queries/<bench>/<unit>/<retriever>/<split>.jsonl
harness.full_scores_rule: the rows keep only the top_n_stored scores, so collect ranks every query again with the harness retriever classes (utils.retrieval_experiments.build_retriever) on the same workload to read the score of every candidate unit; dense vectors and cross-encoder scores come only from the harness cache (encoding and model loading raise, cache files are never written), sparse retrievers are refitted on CPU; every query is checked against its row (top-1 id, rank of the first relevant unit, stored top ids and rounded scores) and any disagreement stops the run
harness.cache_guard: the collect step replaces DenseEncoder.encode and .load, RerankRetriever.load and VectorStore.add with functions that stop the run, and VectorStore.flush with a no-op, on the retriever instances it builds; a target whose harness rows or cache directories (store.json) are missing is skipped and listed in collect/skipped_targets.json

splits.rule: logistic regressions, Youden thresholds and conformal thresholds are fitted on the fit split only (exactly one) and applied unchanged to the evaluate splits; the final_test splits are read only with --final-test, evaluated with the thresholds fitted on the fit split, and nothing is chosen on them; every feature row is checked against the manifest split of its hearing

targets.primary_reason: the production evidence decision: the UDV builder takes the top-1 sentence of the production encoder among the speaker's sentences and labels it semantic_match_high when its cosine reaches [evidence].embedding_threshold
targets.list_reason: declared before any confidence result: the production encoder on the four units of the harness, the two retrievers built on top of it that the harness runs on sentences (cross-encoder rerank and RRF hybrid), and the sparse reference already scored by the harness; any other target is run on request and reported as such
targets.bench_rule: each benchmark is analysed separately: their relevance labels mean different things (masked_quotes: the unit holds the silver quote target; nli: the unit overlaps a chunk the annotator judged the opinion inferable from, retrieved_context_entailment, not global truth)

label.definition: correct is true when the harness rank of the first relevant unit is 1 (order by score descending, candidate index ascending on ties, the argmax rule of the UDV builder)
label.tie_bounds: rank_optimistic == 1 and rank_pessimistic == 1 are written next to the label, so queries whose label depends on tie order can be counted

population.rule: queries with fewer than min_candidates candidate units are left out of every signal and policy comparison: with one candidate the top-1 is relevant by construction (every benchmark query has a relevant unit) and margin and z-score are undefined; they are counted, and the production rule is also reported on all queries including them
population.subsets_definition: multi_candidate: n_units >= min_candidates (the primary population); nontrivial: multi_candidate and n_relevant < n_units, where a wrong top-1 is possible; signal metrics are reported on both, policies on multi_candidate only

signals.definitions: top1_score: the retriever score of the rank-1 unit (cosine for dense retrievers, BM25 or TF-IDF score for sparse ones, fused reciprocal-rank score for RRF, raw cross-encoder logit for rerankers); margin: top1_score minus the score of the rank-2 unit; zscore: (top1_score - mean) / std over the scores of every candidate unit of the query, population std (ddof 0), set to zero_spread_value when std <= 1e-12 * max(1, |mean|), that is when every candidate has the same score up to float rounding (counted as zero_spread); for rerankers the distribution is the reranked top_k units, the only units with a cross-encoder score
signals.direction: every signal is read as higher = more confident; a policy accepts the top-1 when signal >= threshold

entailment.scorers_reason: the primary system declared for the NLI verifier experiment (per-chunk P(entailment) of the 3-way multilingual NLI model); assin2_mdeberta can be added here and scored with the same pairs file
entailment.units_reason: turn units are left out: in the sparse harness runs on train+validation (retrieval_v1_report.json, summaries.<bench>.train+validation.turn.<retriever>.top1_chars) the median top-1 turn has 4,675 to 6,856 characters depending on retriever and benchmark, and the XNLI tokenizer produced 3.28 characters per token on the 319 sentence and window3 smoke pairs of this experiment, so a typical top-1 turn is well past the 512-token limit of both NLI models and the premise would be cut in most pairs
entailment.pair: premise (evidence) = text of the top-1 unit; hypothesis (proposition) = the query text the retriever saw (the masked opinion for masked_quotes, the NLI opinion for nli); one pair per distinct (bench, query, top-1 text) over all targets, pair_id = <bench>:<query_id>#<first 16 hex of sha256(top-1 text)>
entailment.pairs_input: <run_dir>/nli/pairs_input.jsonl, written by the pairs command, which rebuilds the unit texts from the LDS (harness workload) and checks each against the top1_text_sha256 of the features
entailment.scores_location: <run_dir>/nli/pairs/<run_name>/<scorer>.jsonl, written by utils.nli_verifier_experiments pairs --input <pairs_input> --run-name <run_name> --output-dir <run_dir>/nli --scorers <scorers>; the evaluate step records whether the scored input sha256 equals the current pairs_input
entailment.missing_rule: whether a target gets the entailment signal is decided on the fit and evaluate splits only: it gets it when every query of its population in those splits has a score; otherwise the signal and every feature set using it are reported as missing for that target. With --final-test, a signal kept this way must also be scored on every final_test query, and the run is refused otherwise, so the test rows can never change which models are fitted

logistic.feature_sets_reason: scores uses only what the retriever returns; scores_entailment adds the NLI verifier, so the difference measures what entailment adds
logistic.standardize: features centred and scaled with the mean and population std of the fit rows; a constant feature is left unscaled
logistic.class_weight_reason: unweighted, so the probability estimates P(correct) at the base rate of the fit split and the 0.5 policy means what it says

policies.youden_signals: every signal, including the logistic probabilities
policies.youden_rule: threshold maximising TPR - FPR with correct as the positive class on the fit rows (utils.calibrate_threshold.youden_optimum: lowest threshold on ties, midpoint between the lowest kept and the highest excluded score); J = 0 keeps every query and is reported as degenerate
policies.conformal_rule: split conformal on the correct fit queries: with n of them and k = floor(alpha * (n + 1)), the threshold is the k-th smallest of their signal values (no threshold, everything accepted, when k = 0); a new correct query then reaches the threshold with probability at least 1 - alpha if it is exchangeable with the calibration queries. The temporal split and hearing clustering break exchangeability, so the realised recall of correct top-1s on the evaluate split is the measured quantity
policies.probability_rule: logistic.<feature_set> >= probability_threshold, no fitting beyond the regression

production_rule.threshold_keys_reason: embedding_threshold is the cut the UDV builder applies now (semantic_match_high when the top-1 cosine reaches it); previous_embedding_threshold is the 0.47 used until the train-only recalibration of 2026-09-23; both are read from the UDV config at every run and recorded
production_rule.comparison_rule: embedding_threshold (0.45) was calibrated on train hearings only; previous_embedding_threshold (0.47) was calibrated on the 20 hearings of dev20, part of which are validation and test hearings, so its metrics on those splits are partly in-sample. Each production policy entry carries calibration_overlap (the calibration hearings that fall in the evaluated split and their queries); the two cuts are compared only in production_rule.outside_calibration, on the queries of hearings outside every calibration set, and 0.47 is otherwise a historical reference
production_rule.query_text_note: the production builder scores the unmasked LDS opinion; masked_quotes queries are the masked opinion and nli queries are the NLI opinion, so the rule is evaluated on the harness queries, not on the production records
production_rule.score_note: the harness cosine is the dot product of L2-normalized float32 vectors and the builder uses sklearn cosine_similarity on the raw vectors; the two agree up to float32 rounding (not measured here), so only a score within rounding distance of a threshold can fall on the other side of it

embedding_threshold.role: current cut, calibrated on train only
embedding_threshold.description: legacy_random rule of utils.calibrate_threshold on train hearings: unmasked opinion vs its trusted-quote sentence against a random sentence of another train hearing, midpoint of q25(positive) and q75(negative), rounded to 0.45; the hearings it could use are leak_check.hearing_ids_used of the calibration artifact

previous_embedding_threshold.role: historical reference, calibrated on dev20 (hearings of train, validation and test)
previous_embedding_threshold.description: 0.47 was calibrated in udv_v05.ipynb on pairs confirmed by a case-insensitive quote prefix of 6+ words against random pairs (35 pairs from 20 records, per the [evidence] section of dev20_coverage.json), midpoint of q25(positive) and q75(negative), drawn from the hearings of the dev20 run; every hearing of dev20.jsonl is treated as a calibration hearing

evaluation.risk_coverage_rule: queries sorted by signal descending; coverage j/n keeps the first j; risk = error share among them; ties in the signal are resolved by the expected value over every order of the tied queries; AURC = mean risk over j = 1..n; oracle AURC puts every correct query first; e_aurc = AURC - oracle AURC; precision at coverage c keeps the first ceil(c * n) queries, a choice made on the evaluate split itself, so it describes ranking quality and is not a deployable policy
evaluation.bootstrap_unit_reason: opinions of the same hearing share speakers, topic and transcript, so they are not independent; every replicate resamples whole hearings of the evaluate split and, independently, of the fit split
evaluation.bootstrap_intervals: fixed: the thresholds and regressions fitted on the full fit split, applied to each resampled evaluate split; refit: thresholds and regressions refitted on each resampled fit split and applied to the resampled evaluate split of the same replicate, so the interval also carries the fitting uncertainty; paired differences of signal metrics use the same evaluate replicates
evaluation.primary_interval_amendment: Recorded on 2026-09-23, before any confidence result on retrieval outputs was computed: a lower AURC is better, so 'better than top1_score' means the whole paired 95% interval of AURC(signal) - AURC(top1_score) lies below 0 (better_than_reference in the report); for a signal that is fitted (logistic.*) the interval used is the refit one, so it carries the fitting uncertainty; for the raw signals the fixed and refit intervals coincide and the fixed one is reported.
evaluation.primary_declaration: Declared on 2026-09-23, before any confidence result on retrieval outputs was computed. Question: which signal best predicts that the top-1 unit is correct. Primary target: serafim_335m.sentence. Primary metric: validation AURC on the multi_candidate population, per benchmark, with a hearing-bootstrap interval; a signal is said to predict correctness better than top1_score only when the paired 95% interval of its AURC difference excludes 0. ROC AUC, average precision, precision at coverage and every policy are reported next to it. nli is the benchmark the conclusion rests on; masked_quotes (40 validation queries, 142 train) is reported with the same method and its intervals are expected to be too wide for a conclusion. Smoke tests on synthetic inputs and on a few hearings of the harness outputs were run after this declaration.

collect.score_tolerance_reason: harness rows round scores to 5 decimals

run.smoke_rule: collect --hearing-ids writes to <run_name>_smoke unless --run-name is given, and every later step prints and records the hearing filter of each collect report it reads
run.model_loading: none: collect reads the harness caches, pairs only writes text pairs, evaluate works on the saved features; the entailment scores come from utils.nli_verifier_experiments, which records model, revision and label probes in its own report

masked_quotes.candidates: the row's candidate list (the speaker's per-turn sentences), checked against the list rebuilt from the LDS with resolve_hearing_people
masked_quotes.relevance: a unit is relevant when it contains a sentence listed in target_indices (the sentences that agree with the silver target sentence enclosing the trusted quote prefix)

filters: at least one sentence unit of the speaker overlaps a located chunk segment
nli.candidates: rebuilt from person_resolution.turn_indices with split_into_turns and split_sentences on each turn, the resolution rechecked with resolve_person_speech on the NLI person name
nli.relevance: a unit is relevant when its character span overlaps the recorded span (chosen occurrence) of any segment of any located chunk of the opinion; the label says the opinion was judged inferable from the four retrieved chunks together (retrieved_context_entailment), not that each overlapping unit supports it

units.definitions: sentence: one candidate sentence; windowN: N consecutive candidate sentences of one turn, stride 1, a turn with fewer than N sentences gives one unit with all of them, text joined by a space, span from the first sentence start to the last sentence end; turn: the whole turn text (whitespace normalized, including stage directions and parts shorter than a sentence), only turns with at least one candidate sentence

serafim_335m.card_notes: config_sentence_transformers.json: prompts {} and default_prompt_name null, so no prefix; modules: Transformer (BertModel, hidden 1024) + mean Pooling, no Normalize module; sentence_bert_config.json max_seq_length 128 (production value, kept so vectors equal the build_udvs cache); trained with AnglELoss on STS.

serafim_335m_ir.card_notes: prompts {} and default_prompt_name null, no prefix in the card usage; Transformer (BertModel, 1024) + mean Pooling, no Normalize; max_seq_length 128; train-config.yaml: GISTEmbedLoss on unicamp-dl/mmarco portuguese pairs, base bertimbau-335m.

serafim_900m.card_notes: prompts {} and default_prompt_name null, no prefix; Transformer (DebertaV2Model, hidden 1536) + mean Pooling, no Normalize; max_seq_length 128; train-config.yaml base albertina-900m-ptpt (European Portuguese base), CoSENT on STS.

e5_large.card_notes: README: each input must start with 'query: ' or 'passage: '; 'query: '/'passage: ' for asymmetric passage retrieval, 'query: ' on both sides for symmetric similarity; the asymmetric pair is used because the query (an opinion summary) and the passages (transcript speech) differ in length and register. No config_sentence_transformers.json prompts in the snapshot, so the prefixes are prepended to the text here. Modules: XLMRobertaModel (1024) + mean Pooling + Normalize; max_seq_length 512.

bge_m3.card_notes: README: 'the BGE-M3 model no longer requires adding instructions to the queries'; dense vectors from sentence-transformers: XLMRobertaModel (1024) + CLS Pooling + Normalize; max_seq_length 8192 (native, kept; a batch never exceeds token_budget tokens, so one 8192-token sequence runs alone). Sparse and ColBERT heads (sparse_linear.pt, colbert_linear.pt) are not used.

mpnet.card_notes: no prompts in config_sentence_transformers.json and no prefix in the card; XLMRobertaModel (768) + mean Pooling, no Normalize; max_seq_length 128; paraphrase model (symmetric).

minilm.card_notes: no prompts and no prefix; BertModel (384) + mean Pooling, no Normalize; max_seq_length 128; paraphrase model (symmetric).

hybrid_rrf.choice: declared before any retrieval result was computed: BM25 fitted on the speaker's units (the sparse design the benchmarks were built around) fused with the production encoder, so the hybrid measures what lexical evidence adds to the encoder already in use; another dense component may only be chosen on train

rerank_bge.card_notes: config.json: XLMRobertaForSequenceClassification with id2label {0: LABEL_0}, a single relevance logit (higher = more relevant), no sbert_ce_default_activation_function; README scores with max_length=512 and maps to [0, 1] with sigmoid only optionally. The raw logit is used (activation Identity), which gives the same order as the sigmoid without saturated ties. No query instruction for this normal (non-LLM) reranker.

rerank_mmarco.card_notes: config.json: XLMRobertaForSequenceClassification, id2label {0: LABEL_0}, a single logit, sbert_ce_default_activation_function Identity; tokenizer model_max_length 512; trained on machine-translated mMARCO (includes pt).

evaluation.multiple_comparisons: holm, one family per question: E1 (retrievers) compares every retriever with baseline_retriever on the same unit kind, one family per benchmark, split group, unit kind and test (McNemar on acc@1, sign-flip on reciprocal rank); E2 (units) compares every unit kind with baseline_unit for the same retriever on the paired lift (hit@1 minus n_relevant / n_units), one family per benchmark, split group and retriever; no test crosses both the retriever and the unit kind, and every adjusted p-value records its family
evaluation.multiple_comparisons_amendment: Recorded on 2026-09-23, before any summarize run that included a dense retriever: the first version tested every (retriever, unit) pair against serafim_335m on sentences with raw acc@1 and MRR in one family per benchmark and split group, which mixed the retriever and unit questions and rewarded larger units for their higher chance of holding a relevant unit (random_acc_at_1 0.015 on B1 sentences vs 0.455 on B1 turns; 1,365 of 3,222 B2 turn queries have every unit relevant); the only summarize report written before this change (retrieval_v1_report.json of the sparse run) had no baseline rows, so no comparison had been computed
evaluation.tie_policy: order by score descending, candidate index ascending on ties (the argmax rule of the UDV builder); rank_optimistic and rank_pessimistic bound the rank of the first relevant unit over every tie order

cache.batch_size_note: batch sizes measured on 2026-09-22 (Apple M5, MPS, fp32, serafim-335m, 512 sentences): 16 to 32 give about 2.1k tokens/s, 64 about 1.0k and 256 about 0.55k; the batch size changes vectors only at float rounding level

queue.plan: priority order under the measured MPS throughput: every retriever on the sentence unit (E1) and the turn unit, the four units (E2) for the production encoder, the hybrid and the small reranker; windows for other dense models and the large reranker beyond sentences are left for a later step chosen on train
